method: Compared r_w12 (09d_suite.js at 08dd180, 360 lines) with r_w11, using side-by-side crops and pixel diffs in scratchpad/qa12b/. s4 is pixel-identical to w11; s2, s3, v3 and v4 differ by fewer than 90 px. Measurements are PIL box means and luminance profiles, compared as ratios within one image. References: omaat_f60, f7, f11 and f57.

calibration.earlier_issue: w11a/b MED: with the doors closed, a continuous proud plinth ran across the doorway instead of the dark void in f60
calibration.status: fixed. Line 262 now fixes the plinth faces to the shell either side of zo0..zo1, and line 241 adds the black toe-kick. v1 doorway: L23 against field L82 (0.28x); f60: L18 against L64 (0.28x). The plinth reads L57 (0.70x the field); f60 reads 45-50 (0.70-0.78x).

calibration.earlier_issue: w11b LOW: plinth too light (0.84x the field); far LOD had no plinth
calibration.status: fixed. Line 240 sets #33312b, now 0.70x the field. Line 354 adds the far plinth, which v5 shows under the far unit.

calibration.earlier_issue: w11a LOW: chrome foot strip barely legible
calibration.status: fixed. Line 253 makes it 0.015 tall. In the v1 profile it is a 3-4 px band at L169 (2.1x the slats); f7 gives about 2.8x.

calibration.earlier_issue: w11a LOW: flute groove only 23 % of the pitch
calibration.status: fixed in geometry. Line 249 uses 0.016 slats on a 0.026 pitch (38 %). v1 relief p90/p10 is 1.34, and f60 measured over the same band is 1.25. The grooves are still light, though: groove/slat is 67/91 = 0.74, against about 25/72 = 0.35 in f60 (see issues).

calibration.earlier_issue: w11b LOW: stipple moire on the fluted leaves at grazing angles
calibration.status: not fixed. The q02 right-hand leaves (qa12b/q02R_cmp.png, x 780-930) still show the chain or scale pattern, identical to w11.

calibration.earlier_issue: w11a/b LOW: hard triangular wedge end faces on the console module
calibration.status: not fixed. Line 173 is still a straight 0.52 gExtrude. s4 is pixel-identical to w11 and shows the same doorstop end at x 520-545. It is also visible in v2 at x 130-240.

calibration.earlier_issue: w11a/b LOW: turned-down duvet corner reads as a flat decal
calibration.status: partly fixed. Line 308 makes it thicker and greyer, and line 309 adds a ridge along the hypotenuse, so it now reads as a triangle in q04 (qa12b/q04bed_cmp.png). It is still a plate lying on the duvet in the corner, though. In f57 that corner is bare sheet, and the folded flap lies on the other side of the diagonal (see issues).

calibration.earlier_issue: w11a LOW: aisle drape stopped 0.06 short of the duvet foot
calibration.status: fixed. Line 310 runs the full dl, and q04 / s5 show no notch.

calibration.earlier_issue: Out of scope: ottoman tweed too light, hard sun patches, plaques
calibration.status: unchanged (other owners). The q03 ottoman is beige, against the charcoal tweed of f11; q04 still has sun lozenges.

details.detail: Screen wall: 43-in screen, r 0.10 rounded wing, angled pier with pill mirror and lamp
details.refs: q03 vs omaat_f11. Wing/screen is 38/312 px = 0.12 (f11 0.15); mirror height 154 px = 0.47 m (f11 about 0.45).

details.detail: Centre pair: board, edge strips, divider lowered and raised
details.refs: s3, v3, v4, q02 vs omaat_f32 / f5, tpa_06 (unchanged since w11)
Cap/field is v1 189/82 = 2.30, against f60 163/64 = 2.55. The hue is the accepted middle.

details.detail: Aisle leaves: frame, slats, LED, pulls, chrome foot
details.refs: v1 / s6 vs f60 / f7. The chrome strip is now legible. The grooves are too light (0.74x against 0.35x), and the leaves show moire at grazing angles in q02.
s6 / s1 vs f7, up_34: fixed boxes with grip slots, doorway open to the floor.
v1 vs f60: void/field 0.28 against 0.28 and plinth/field 0.70 against 0.70-0.78. The void is wider than in f60 (0.61 of the closed pair, against 0.40).

details.detail: Window console: tray, module, keypad, handset
details.refs: s4, q04, v2 vs f57 / f7. The wedge end faces are still hard.

details.detail: Seat in niche: back, flap, header fillets, lamps, armrest
Bed: pad, duvet, fold, drape, pillows, belt
details.refs: q04, s5 vs f57. The fold is visible now, but the corner logic is inverted.
q03 vs f11. The fabric colour is out of scope.
v5: the plinth is now present.

issues.issue: Stipple moire persists on the fluted leaves at cabin distance and grazing angles: a chain or scale pattern instead of ribs. It is the most visible remaining suite artefact in the cabin views.
issues.evidence: qa12b/q02R_cmp.png (q02 x 780-930, y 150-450), identical in w11 and w12. Line 249 makes the slats 0.005 proud on a 0.004 groove backing (line 247), which leaves sub-pixel steps that alias and probably cause shadow acne.
issues.fix: Line 249: drop the slats to 0.0025 proud (gBox(0.0025, ...) at x + 0.0032) so the shadow steps halve. Better, for the cabin LOD only: when the suite is not in close-up, replace the slat loop with one quad that carries a mip-mapped 0.026-period stripe (a LAYER or atlasUV slot), and keep the geometry for studio and close views. Ask the lighting owner whether the shadow receiver bias covers 5 mm steps.

issues.issue: The flute grooves are too light. The real leaves read as broad slats separated by narrow near-black slots. Here the groove is a mid-tone, which flattens the field into pinstripes at close range.
issues.evidence: v1 row y 250: slat L91, groove L67 (0.74x). f60 row y 600: slat about L72, groove about L25 (0.35x).
issues.fix: Line 19: fFluteGap c '#393730' -> '#24221d' (about 0.5x the slat). Re-check moire in q02 at the same time; if the darker groove worsens it, pair this with the line-249 proud reduction above.

issues.issue: The console module still has hard flat triangular end faces, a doorstop look. The real module ends are radiused and blend into the console top.
issues.evidence: s4 x 520-545, y 270-300 (pixel-identical to w11); v2 x 130-240. f57 / f7 show rounded ends.
issues.fix: Line 173: extrude 0.46 long at M4.trs(0, 0, -0.65), then cap each end with a softened copy: for (const s of [-1, 1]) B.add(gRBox(xs1 - xo - 0.004, (y0 + 0.012) - 0.655, 0.03, 0.012, 2), M4.trs((xs1 + xo) / 2, (y0 + 0.012 + 0.655) / 2 - 0.004, -0.68 + s * 0.245), SEATMAT.fConsole); The square box top sits under the wedge's sloped face at the cap; the r 0.012 corners remove the knife edge.

issues.issue: The duvet fold is geometrically inverted. The model lays the greyer flap triangle ON the head-end aisle corner. In f57 that corner is folded back: it shows the bare sheet, and the double-layer flap lies on the other side of the diagonal, toward the window and the foot. The plate on the corner therefore still reads as a sticker.
issues.evidence: qa12b/q04bed_cmp.png: the triangle (L about 225) sits inside the duvet corner, and the duvet edge continues square around it. f57: the head-aisle corner shows white sheet up to the diagonal fold.
issues.fix: Line 308: keep the triangle but give it the pad material, { c: '#f0efea', r: 0.9, l: LAYER.fabric }, at y 0.5315, so it reads as exposed sheet. Then add the flap as the mirror across the hypotenuse: B.add(gExtrude([[xe - 0.36, -dz0 + 0.04], [xe - 0.06, -dz0 + 0.34], [xe - 0.36, -dz0 + 0.34]], 0.014), M4.trs(0, 0.533, 0, 0, -Math.PI / 2), { c: '#c4c0b8', r: 0.95, l: LAYER.fabric }). Keep the line-309 ridge on the diagonal.

issues.issue: Doorway proportion: with the doors closed, the void spans 0.61 of the closed leaf pair, against 0.40 in f60. With the doors open, f7 shows a gap of about 0.95 leaf width, while the model's is 1.28 (0.64 opening, 0.50 leaves).
issues.evidence: v1 row y 400: void x 262-414 (152 px) under leaves x 214-465 (251 px). f60 row y 860: void x 360-764 (404 px) under leaves x 65-1075 (1010 px). f7: gap x 365-760 against right leaf x 760-1180.
issues.fix: Line 231: narrow the opening to about 0.50 by making the leaves 0.57 wide, rather than shrinking the walk-in. Line 243 open: [[-L + 0.10, -L + 0.67], [-1.03, -0.46]]; zo0 = -L + 0.67, zo1 = -1.03 (opening 0.50); closed: [[zm - 0.57, zm], [zm, zm + 0.57]], and line 244 flanks follow zm +/- 0.57. Line 264 slots at -L + 0.25 and -0.62. Line 352 far leaves likewise. The slat pitch stays 0.026, so each leaf gets about 18 slats. Confidence medium, since both photos are perspective views from above.

issues.issue: The doorway void and toe-kick are cool blue-black, where the real void is a warm brown-black (carpet in shadow).
issues.fix: Line 241: use { c: '#16130f', r: 0.95 } instead of SEATMAT.black.

issues.issue: Out of scope, noted only: the ottoman tweed is beige (q03) where f11 shows dark charcoal; hard sun lozenges on the bed (q04); large navy plaques.

questions: Should the leaves widen to about 0.57 (opening about 0.50) to match the void and gap proportions in f60 and f7, or is the 0.64 walk-in opening a deliberate choice for camera walking?
Should the flute field switch to a mip-mapped stripe at cabin distance? That is the only remaining way to kill the q02 moire without losing the close-up relief.
